title: A normal residual model cut mean squared heat-sum error by 50.5% against a fitted cutoff in an SST smoothing test at 314 ocean pixels in 2019-2025
abstract: The CRW outlook uses a lower heat cutoff to offset loss of daily SST variation. We tested a different method for expected heat totals. We drew 360 reef cells and kept 314 northeast OISST pixels with complete 2010-2025 data. We set a warm-month reference and fitted monthly residual means and standard deviations in 2010-2018. A centred 31-day SST mean was the known smooth signal. We used a normal first moment to estimate the full anomaly on days that cross the 1 C cutoff, then summed it over 84 days. In 2019-2025 its mean squared error was 0.068, against 0.137 for a globally fitted cutoff and 0.323 for local fitted cutoffs. The error reduction against the global cutoff was 50.5% (95% region and two-year block interval 32.7% to 65.9%). The reduction against local cutoffs was 79.0%. Absolute error rose 0.6% and mean heat was 14.6% too high. The expectation formula is exact under the stated normal model, and no single cutoff gives that formula at all mean temperatures. The fitted residual law is only an approximation. This controlled smoothing test has future SST information. It does not verify CFSv2 forecasts, CRW alert probabilities, or coral bleaching. The reference is not the CRW climatology.

display.caption: Held-out error in an SST smoothing test. All model fitting used 2010-2018.
